slides.title: Slow bearings? Twenty minutes fixes that
slides.sub: The clean and oil routine that keeps them fast

slides.title: What slows bearings
slides.body: Grit scores the raceway, water flushes oil out and starts rust, and old lubricant turns into a paste that drags.

slides.title: Wash, then rinse again
slides.body: Agitate the bearings in a sealed jar of solvent, then move them to a second jar of clean solvent. Skipping the rinse leaves dissolved grime inside.

slides.title: Use a solvent that leaves completely
slides.body: A bearing cleaner, citrus degreaser, white spirit or 99 percent isopropyl alcohol. Keep acetone, petrol, brake cleaner and water away.

slides.title: Dry fully, spin by hand
slides.body: Leftover solvent thins the oil and leftover water starts rust. Never let an air line spin a dry bearing, it runs far beyond its design speed.

slides.title: One drop of oil, not a flood
slides.caption: One drop reaches the raceway and rolls, a flooded bearing holds dust and drags.

slides.text: Less is more with a speed bearing.
